ops.title: Changelog debt: 0.28.0-0.59.0 shipped with no version section
ops.description:
CHANGELOG.md jumps directly from `## [Unreleased]` to `## [0.27.0]`. Every release from 0.28.0 through 0.59.0 landed as a bare `chore(release): sync plugin.json to X.Y.Z [skip ci]` commit with no changelog section — confirmed via `git log --oneline --all | grep 'chore(release)'`. As of the v0.59.0 tag, `## [Unreleased]` already held written-up entries that predate that tag (verified with `git show v0.59.0:CHANGELOG.md`), specifically: the `ledger` entity kind, `cc-notes status --tasks`, and the async-hooks perf rewrite (float_note_context/check_note_staleness/record_user_answers going async_=True). All three are live in the currently-installed v0.59.0 binary (e.g. `cc-notes ledger --help` succeeds), so this is already-shipped functionality that was never cut into a version header — not new work.

Reconstructing which of the 30 untagged releases (0.28.0-0.59.0) each backlog entry actually shipped in needs per-entry archaeology (bisecting when each feature's code landed vs. which `chore(release)` commit followed it). Guessing versions would misdate the entries the same way promoting them wholesale into a current release would.

Acceptance: every tagged version from 0.28.0 onward has a `## [x.y.z]` CHANGELOG section (even if terse, e.g. a one-line summary where per-PR detail can't be reconstructed), and `## [Unreleased]` holds only content that is genuinely not yet released in any tag.
